attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills estimate is now twofold: prove the rich-cone hypothesis for the locked Wilson/core algebra near reflected hairpin collars, and prove the boundary Gram factor B is validly isolated from the actual RG/collar limit. Without richness, nonzero K suggests an obstruction but is not yet a proof of OS failure for realized observables.
steps: Start with regulated positivity Q_{a,L}(f,c)>=0. For fixed collar delta, RG convergence of reflected finite matrix entries gives N^{(delta)}(F)>=0 in the continuum because the positive semidefinite matrix cone is closed.

Let delta down to zero. The formal closed-cone argument alone gives positivity of the collar-limit matrix N, not of the intended target matrix M, because boundary singularities may relate them by N=B circ M + A.

Use diagonal trace continuity on locked Wilson observables. If A is a positive additive boundary contact, then A_{ii}=0 for all i; Cauchy-Schwarz gives A_{ij}=0. Therefore additive positive contacts cannot be the surviving obstruction once the diagonal trace theorem is valid.

The remaining relation is M=B^{[-1]} circ N. If B^{[-1]} is a positive Schur multiplier on the relevant matrices, then M>=0 follows from N>=0. If this must hold for all positive matrices, the Schur product theorem requires B^{[-1]}>=0.

Combine B>=0 from the boundary Gram representation with B^{[-1]}>=0. For a normalized two-by-two principal minor, B=[[1,b],[conj(b),1]] and B^{[-1]}=[[1,1/b],[1/conj(b),1]] being positive forces |b|<=1 and |1/b|<=1, hence |b|=1; Cauchy-Schwarz then makes b_i and b_j collinear. Repeating over pairs makes B rank one and K=0.

The correction in this cycle is that the universal Schur step is stronger than the physical hypothesis unless the realized collar OS cone is rich. Therefore the valid bridge lemma must include richness of Wilson hairpin matrix directions, or replace universal positivity by an explicit realized finite-matrix determinant falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation contains valid finite-dimensional linear algebra, but it still assumes analytic inputs not established by the branch: collar trace existence for mixed Wilson products, positivity of the additive contact sector, Gram representation of the multiplicative anomaly, and enough realized OS matrices to upgrade reciprocal Schur positivity to rank-one boundary triviality.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Rich-Cone Boundary Gram Test

assumptions: Each cutoff theory is reflection positive on the gauge-invariant lattice/cutoff algebra, so N_delta >= 0 for every finite family and coefficient vector.

The RG compactness topology dominates finite reflected collar probes: for each fixed delta > 0 and finite F, N_delta(F) has a continuum limit N(F) and positivity passes by closedness of the positive matrix cone.

Diagonal trace continuity is valid on the locked Wilson core: N_{ii}->M_{ii} after the prescribed individual Wilson renormalizations, so any positive additive contact A with zero diagonal vanishes by Cauchy-Schwarz.
The multiplicative boundary anomaly is Gram-positive: B_{ij}=<b_i,b_j>_partial with B_{ii}>0, representing a possible boundary Hilbert sector produced by collar collapse.

Rich-cone hypothesis: for every pair i,j in a dense Wilson hairpin core, the set of realized positive collar matrices N contains enough two-by-two rank-one and small positive perturbation directions that a Schur multiplier preserving positivity on all realized N must pass the usual two-by-two Schur positivity tests.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms S_{a,L} evaluated on the fixed collar algebra T_delta A_+ of gauge-invariant local composites and Wilson hairpin observables, with finite OS matrices N_delta=(S_{a,L}(Theta T_delta F_i,T_delta F_j))_{ij}.

target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions S on the locked zero-collar algebra A_+, with intended matrices M=(S(Theta F_i,F_j))_{ij} generating the physical Hilbert space, vacuum vector, and positive Hamiltonian by the Osterwalder-Schrader quotient.

controlled interface: convergence of every finite reflected collar matrix entry N_delta -> N in the cutoff-removal topology, plus a trace comparison N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij} where A is an additive boundary contact matrix and B is a normalized multiplicative boundary Gram factor from reflected Wilson hairpins.

same-theory condition: the zero-collar algebra A_+ and its renormalized Wilson-loop/composite observables are fixed before taking delta -> 0; only diagonal congruences already included in the locked observable normalization are allowed, while pair-dependent boundary sectors, cusp factors, or contact counterterms define a different theory.

equations.label: collar OS matrix
equations.valid_when: T_delta F_i have support in a positive-time collar separated from the reflection plane and regulated reflection positivity has survived the fixed-collar cutoff limit.

equations.label: boundary trace decomposition
equations.valid_when: The collar limit exists entrywise for the locked finite Wilson/core family and boundary singularities split into multiplicative Wilson hairpin factors plus additive contact terms.

equations.label: positive additive contacts vanish
equations.valid_when: The contact contribution is itself a positive semidefinite OS boundary form and diagonal trace continuity has already removed all diagonal boundary excess.

equations.label: same-theory target from collar limit
equations.valid_when: There are no additive contacts, B has no zero entries on the chosen finite core, and the intended target normalization has not absorbed pair-dependent factors.

equations.label: rank-one obstruction invariant
equations.latex: K_{ik;jl}=\log B_{ij}+\log B_{kl}-\log B_{il}-\log B_{kj};\qquad K\equiv0\iff B_{ij}=r_i\overline{r_j}
equations.valid_when: A consistent logarithm is chosen on a connected finite core with nonzero B entries; the equivalence is local on finite matrices and modulo diagonal congruence phases.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find four locked Wilson hairpin observables with a valid collar limit and nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio K, or find a two-by-two realized collar matrix N for which B^{[-1]} circ N has a negative determinant.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma identifies the missing analytic obligation between formal closed-cone positivity and full same-theory OS positivity: either prove boundary Gram triviality on a rich dense Wilson core, or exhibit a nonrank-one Gram factor as a concrete finite-dimensional falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let A_+ be the locked gauge-invariant positive-time Wilson/core test algebra and let T_delta move each observable into a collar t >= delta. Suppose the cutoff-removal topology is valid for all finite reflected collar OS matrix entries, so the collar matrices N_delta(F) converge to positive matrices N(F). Suppose further that the intended zero-collar target matrix M(F) is related to N(F) by a multiplicative boundary Gram factor B(F), N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}, after additive positive contacts have vanished by diagonal trace continuity. If the realized family of collar OS matrices is locally rich enough to contain all two-dimensional rank-one perturbation directions around each pair of Wilson hairpins, then OS positivity of the intended same-theory target for all finite F forces B to be rank one on the locked Wilson core. Equivalently, the logarithmic cross-ratio K_{ik;jl}=log B_{ij}+log B_{kl}-log B_{il}-log B_{kj} must vanish; any nonzero K is a finite-matrix falsifier of the same-theory OS bridge.

assumptions: The same-theory OS claim quantifies over all locked observables, but not over arbitrary abstract positive matrices unless those matrices are approximable by observables.
The boundary Gram factor is pair-dependent before the same-theory test; diagonal congruence factors are treated as harmless observable normalizations.
The locked algebra contains small linear combinations and products needed to polarize two-by-two matrix entries.
definitions: realized OS cone C_B: the set of all finite collar-limit matrices N(F) generated by locked Wilson/core families F after cutoff removal and collar collapse.
universal Schur test: the demand that B^{[-1]} circ P >= 0 for every positive matrix P of the same size.
realized Schur test: the weaker but physically relevant demand that B^{[-1]} circ N >= 0 for every N in C_B.
richness witness: a family of Wilson/core probes whose OS matrices approximate enough rank-one two-by-two directions to make the realized Schur test equivalent to the universal Schur test.

equations.label: realized versus universal positivity
equations.latex: B^{[-1]}\circ N\ge0\ \forall N\in C_B\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad B^{[-1]}\circ P\ge0\ \forall P\ge0
equations.valid_when: The realized cone C_B is a proper subcone of the full positive semidefinite cone.

equations.label: two-by-two determinant falsifier
equations.valid_when: A realized positive collar matrix N satisfies |N_{12}|^2/(N_{11}N_{22})>|B_{12}|^2/(B_{11}B_{22}).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If no observable family can approximate the two-by-two directions needed to test B^{[-1]}, then the rank-one theorem is only a sufficient criterion, not a necessary same-theory obstruction.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This caveat prevents the branch from overstating the rank-one conclusion and turns the next step into a measurable richness or realized-counterexample problem.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The earlier universal Schur-multiplier argument is valid only if the realized collar OS matrix cone is rich. Without this richness assumption, a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor B is not automatically a falsifier, because the dynamics might realize only a narrow subcone on which B^{[-1]} preserves positivity. Thus the proof must either establish cone richness/density for Wilson hairpins or compute an actual realized finite-matrix violation.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this branch if the locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra cannot be shown to realize enough two-by-two OS matrix directions and no explicit determinant falsifier can be computed from hairpin collar limits.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves either (i) rich-cone density for the Wilson hairpin core plus B rank-one/K=0, yielding same-theory OS positivity, or (ii) a concrete nonrank-one B with a realized N making det(B^{[-1]} circ N)<0.
control_decision.reason: The branch remains productive: it converted the boundary Gram obstruction into a sharper theorem with an explicit missing richness assumption, rather than repeating the closed-cone argument. This gives a concrete promotion path and a concrete falsifier path.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge now factors into fixed-collar closed-cone passage, zero-collar trace decomposition, additive-contact vanishing, and a rich-cone boundary Gram triviality test.
dependency_updates.status: formal core valid; analytic collar and richness estimates open

dependency_updates.description: The locked algebra must contain a dense Wilson hairpin/core sector closed under finite linear combinations and products sufficient to polarize two-by-two OS matrix directions.
The topology must control not only fixed reflected collar entries but also their delta -> 0 trace comparison and the extraction of B, A from mixed Wilson products.
A candidate multiplicative boundary anomaly must be represented as a positive Gram kernel B and tested by the reciprocal Schur multiplier on the realized OS cone.

falsifiers: A direct two-by-two realized Wilson hairpin matrix N with N>=0 but det(B^{[-1]} circ N)<0; this is the cleanest finite falsifier of the same-theory OS bridge.

A four-observable Wilson hairpin family with nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio K after all allowed individual renormalizations, together with richness witnesses showing that this K is tested by realized OS matrices.

A positive collar limit whose zero-collar comparison requires an additive contact A with zero diagonal but nonzero off-diagonal; this would falsify the assumed positive-boundary-contact decomposition itself.
A boundary Gram factor B that is nonrank-one but the realized OS cone C_B is too small to detect it; this falsifier targets the necessity of the rank-one conclusion rather than OS positivity itself.
A change of Wilson-loop renormalization at the reflection plane that absorbs B by pair-dependent counterterms; this preserves a modified positive theory but violates the same-theory condition.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 193 found an important correction to the previous rank-one conclusion. The finite-dimensional theorem is valid when reciprocal Schur positivity is required on a rich enough cone of OS matrices; then a positive boundary Gram factor must be rank one and K=0. But the physical problem only gives realized Wilson OS matrices, not arbitrary positive matrices. Thus the next real bridge lemma must include a rich-cone/density hypothesis, or else produce an actual realized determinant falsifier. This is substantive progress because it prevents overclaiming: nonzero boundary covariance is a decisive same-theory obstruction only after the locked Wilson algebra can test it.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work on a two-observable Wilson hairpin model: define F_1,F_2 with coincident boundary footprints, compute the normalized collar matrix N and candidate Gram factor B to first nontrivial boundary-OPE order, and test whether the determinant inequality det(B^{[-1]} circ N)>=0 is automatic, violated, or dependent on a richness/density assumption.
